transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know from the capital-planning agenda, we have the battery-storage installation proposal for the distribution campus up for review today. The proposal lists a $6 million purchase price under an ownership model. Before I make my approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you — FP&A, tax, treasury, and legal — on any relevant information you have regarding this project. Let's start with whoever is ready.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the project cash-flow model this morning. At the company's required return hurdle, the economically approvable purchase price is exactly $4,800,000. The $6,000,000 proposal does not pass the model's hurdle. I should note that I have not yet attached the completed model to the investment-review file, but I'm sharing these findings now so they're on the record before Maya's decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important tax consideration before we proceed. I received a tax memorandum this week confirming that the applicable 30% investment credit for this battery-storage installation is available only if the company owns the equipment. If we were to structure this as a lease instead of a purchase, that credit would be unavailable. I have not yet circulated the memorandum to the planning team, but given that the proposal is currently under an ownership model, the credit would apply. This is relevant to the economics of the project and should be factored into any decision Maya makes today.

transcript.text: I need to share a critical treasury and funding update before Maya's decision. In today's rolling cash forecast, I confirmed that only $2,000,000 can be deployed from cash without breaching our operating-liquidity floor. The remaining $2,800,000 of the renegotiated $4,800,000 purchase price can be funded through an available five-year term-loan facility. The approved closing funding split is fixed at $2,000,000 cash plus $2,800,000 term-loan funding. I should note that the 30% investment credit Elena mentioned is recognized later and does not reduce the required closing funding. I have not yet updated the funding worksheet, but I'm putting this on the record now so Maya has the full funding picture before making her decision.

transcript.text: I need to share an important legal finding before Maya's decision. In reviewing the utility interconnection agreement this week, I found that energization of the battery-storage system requires a $400,000 performance bond and a signed commissioning certificate before the system can be placed in service. These conditions are not yet reflected in the draft approval. The $400,000 performance bond is an additional cost that should be factored into the project economics, and the commissioning certificate requirement is a condition precedent that affects when the system can actually be operational. I'm putting this on the record now so Maya has the complete legal picture before making her decision.
